text: The research field of business administration is centered around the "entire process of organizational operation", covering multiple dimensions such as strategy, human resources, finance, and marketing. The main directions include: Strategic Management: This involves studying the long-term development direction and competitive strategies of enterprises, covering industry analysis, market positioning, resource integration, risk control, etc. For example, how enterprises can formulate global strategies and respond to industry changes (such as digital transformation).Marketing: This focuses on the promotion of products or services and the matching of user needs, including market research, brand building, channel management, digital marketing (such as social media marketing, live-streaming e-commerce), etc. The core is to achieve "value transmission" and "user growth".Human Resources Management: This pays attention to the selection, training, utilization, and retention of internal talents in the organization, covering recruitment and allocation, performance management, salary system design, organizational culture building, and employee relationship management, etc. For example, how to enhance team efficiency through incentive mechanisms.Financial Management: This studies the raising, allocation, monitoring, and appreciation of enterprise funds, including financial statement analysis, investment decisions, financing management, risk management (such as exchange rate risk, credit risk), etc. It is the "financial core" for the stable operation of enterprises.Operational Management: This focuses on the efficient execution of core business of enterprises, involving production planning, supply chain management, quality management, process optimization, etc. For example, lean production in manufacturing and improvement of logistics delivery efficiency in e-commerce enterprises.
